title: Three Stories for a Sleepless Night
deck: A sound behind a wall, a reflection that lingers, and a voice from beneath the bed. Three original tales of things that should not answer back.

sections.title: The room on the other side
paragraphs: The scratching began after the last bus passed the house. Mara knew the sound of mice. Mice hurried and stopped. This moved slowly, from the bedroom door to the window, as though someone were dragging a single fingernail along the other side of the plaster.

At breakfast, she knocked on the wall to show the landlord where it had happened. Three knocks. He looked at the wardrobe, then at the ceiling, and told her the building had no room on that side. Beyond the wall was open air.

That night she moved her bed across the room. The scratching followed. At two in the morning it stopped behind her pillow, although the pillow was now against the opposite wall. She held her breath. From inside the plaster, someone held theirs.

Mara found a photograph in the hallway the next morning: the house before the extension, a garden where her bedroom stood, and a woman looking through a window that no longer existed. On the back, in fresh pencil, were three words: Stop knocking back.

sections.title: The last person in the mirror
paragraphs: Eli always covered the hallway mirror before a storm. It was one of his grandmother's habits, and he had kept it for the same reason he kept her teacups: some things were easier to preserve than explain.
One evening the cloth slipped. Lightning showed him his own reflection halfway up the stairs. Eli was standing at the bottom. In the dark between flashes he heard a shoe touch the next step.

He reached for the cloth, but his reflection put a finger to its lips. There was someone behind it in the glass, a tall shape folded to fit beneath the ceiling. The reflection was not warning Eli to be quiet. It was asking him to listen.

Eli covered the mirror and spent the night in the kitchen. In the morning the stairs were dry and empty, except for two wet footprints on the inside of the glass. One faced up the stairs. The other faced out.

sections.title: The question under the bed
paragraphs: Nora dropped her phone beneath the bed and called it from the kitchen. In the bedroom, the ringtone stopped after one note. Then her own recorded voice said, very softly, 'I'm here.'

She checked the screen on the kitchen phone. The call was still connecting. She ended it. The voice in the bedroom kept talking, listing ordinary things: the coat on the chair, the book on the floor, the hand resting beside the mattress.

Nora had left the bedroom door open. From the hall she could see the coat and the book. She could not see a hand. She stepped backwards until her shoulders touched the front door, keeping the gap beneath the bed in sight.

Her missing phone slid into the hallway. Its screen displayed an incoming call from her number. Nora did not answer. A moment later, the voice beneath the bed asked a new question: 'If you're out there, who is lying up here?'

sections.title: Keep the light on for one more page
paragraphs: These tales use ordinary spaces as their starting point. The fear comes from one small detail refusing to behave as expected. For more fictional encounters, explore the related videos and stories below.

title: Five Camera-Inspired Horror Stories
deck: A familiar room can become a different place when you watch the recording. Five fictional scenes about cameras that seem to know more than their owners.

sections.title: The visitor between frames
paragraphs: The doorbell camera saved an image every time someone approached the porch. For seven nights, each image showed the same empty chair. On the eighth, the chair was turned towards the house.
Jon put a coin on the seat and watched the live feed. Nothing moved. In the saved photograph, a pale hand was holding the coin. The notification arrived a second later: Familiar face detected.

sections.title: The floor that was not there
paragraphs: An elevator repair technician reviewed a recording after a complaint about an unexpected stop. The camera showed a passenger pressing five, then stepping into a corridor on floor six. The building had only five floors.

The passenger returned before the doors closed. She was older than she had been a moment before. She turned towards the camera and shook her head, once. The technician deleted the recording. The next morning, the button for six had appeared.

sections.title: The other window
paragraphs: A couple left a camera pointing at their living-room window while they travelled. Every afternoon it showed the neighbour watering plants. Every night it showed the reflection of their empty sofa.

On the final evening, the reflected sofa held two people. The couple watched themselves sit perfectly still in their own house. Behind the real sofa, the camera's small red light began to blink. In the hotel, the television switched on.

sections.title: One step behind
paragraphs: The trail camera was supposed to photograph foxes. Instead it collected pictures of a lone hiker, always at the same bend in the path, always carrying a yellow backpack. The dates were different. The pose was identical.
The ranger went to retrieve it. When he opened the case, the camera took one last picture. On the screen, the hiker stood behind him, without the backpack. The ranger was wearing it.

sections.title: The room after midnight
paragraphs: A motion alert woke Asha at 12:03. Her camera showed her bedroom exactly as it was: lamp off, curtains closed, a glass beside the bed. Only the bed was empty.

She was lying in it. She waved a hand in front of the lens. On the recording, the curtains opened instead. Something outside leaned towards the window. Asha reached for the lamp, and a hand in the dark found the switch first.

sections.title: When the screen becomes the storyteller
paragraphs: A camera seems reliable because it records what we miss. In horror fiction, that promise can turn against the viewer: the image becomes the uncertain witness, and the familiar room becomes the mystery. These scenes are invented, not evidence of paranormal events. Watch the related Dark Echo videos for more stories built around unexpected recordings.

title: Ten Fictional Encounters After Dark
deck: A countdown of imagined horror scenes, from an empty lift to a mirror that refuses to follow. Read slowly; the last detail changes each scene.

sections.title: The elevator shadow
paragraphs: A woman stepped into an empty lift. The camera showed a shadow enter with her, though the doors had already closed. At her floor, she stepped out. The shadow stayed behind and pressed the button for her apartment.

sections.title: The hospital curtain
paragraphs: The abandoned ward had been stripped of its beds. One privacy curtain still hung from its rail. When the explorers pulled it aside, they found only a patch of warm floor. Behind them, an invisible monitor began to count a heartbeat.

sections.title: The forest reply
paragraphs: Lost in the trees, Tom called his brother's name. A voice answered from the left. He called again. This time it came from the right, closer. Then his brother's phone rang in his pocket. The message said: Don't follow my voice.

sections.title: The doll on the shelf
paragraphs: The doll faced the wall each morning. June turned it towards the room before bed, convinced the shelf was uneven. One night she stayed awake to watch. The doll did not move. Every other object in the room slowly turned to face it.

sections.title: The spare key
paragraphs: The locked door opened at three. A man stood in the hall holding a key, wearing the coat Ben had buried his father in. Ben could not see his face. The man hung the key on its hook and whispered, 'Someone else has the spare.'

sections.title: The delayed reflection
paragraphs: She raised her hand. The reflection waited. She lowered it. The reflection raised its own hand and pressed one finger against the glass. A tiny crack appeared on her side, and cold air began to move into the room.

sections.title: The final stair
paragraphs: There were twelve stairs to the bedroom. Simon counted thirteen in the dark. At the top he found a door he did not recognise. His mother's voice came from behind it, asking him to come down for breakfast. It had been midnight when he started climbing.

sections.title: The empty shoes
paragraphs: Footsteps crossed the hallway each night. The landlord blamed the pipes until the tenant left a pair of shoes outside the door. In the morning they were worn through at the soles. Inside each one was a folded note: A little further tomorrow.

sections.title: The baby monitor
paragraphs: The baby was asleep beside her when the monitor crackled. From the empty nursery came a soothing voice, humming the song she always sang. Then her own voice said, 'Don't wake him.' Her baby opened his eyes and looked towards the speaker.

sections.title: The face at the lens
paragraphs: The night camera recorded a face inches from its lens. No body entered the frame. The owner turned the camera towards the wall, thinking it was a reflection. The next recording showed the back of the same head. It was looking into the room.

sections.title: One ordinary detail, one impossible change
paragraphs: These are fictional scenes written for entertainment, not a list of verified recordings. Their shared device is a small violation of expectation: an extra stair, a delayed movement, a familiar voice from the wrong place. The related videos below explore the same kind of unsettling storytelling.
